memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the seventh day wash your clothes and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp." The Lord said to Moses, "You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the community are to count all the people and animals that were captured." - Num 31:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After seven days, after washing, after the purification was complete, the soldiers could come back into the camp. There is something tender in that little phrase: "Then you may come into the camp." The purpose of all the cleansing was not to keep people away forever, but to bring them home clean, restored to fellowship with the community and with God.

This is the heartbeat of God through all of Scripture. He does not cleanse us in order to keep us at a distance; He cleanses us in order to draw us near. The whole story of the Bible moves toward reconciliation — God making a way for defiled people to dwell in His presence again. Every washing in the old covenant whispered of the day when God would wash His people fully and welcome them home for good.

That day came in Jesus. Through His blood, we who were once far off have been brought near (Eph 2:13). We no longer wait outside the camp for seven days; the way into God's presence stands open. And there is a further comfort here: even Jesus suffered "outside the camp" for us, bearing our disgrace so that we could be brought in (Heb 13:12-13). What the soldiers waited days to receive, we receive freely and forever in Christ — a welcome home that will never be withdrawn.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of God as keeping you at a distance, or drawing you near?
2. What does it mean to you that Christ suffered "outside the camp" for your sake?
3. How can you rest today in the welcome God has given you in Jesus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Loving Father, thank You that You cleanse me not to push me away but to bring me home. Thank You that Jesus made the way, and that I am welcomed near forever. Amen.
